Sāyaṇa
(14th century A. D.; d.A. D. 1387)
------------------------------------------
If it was left to शङ्कर (A. D. 788-820) to unravel the mysteries of the Vedāntic scriptures—especially the prasthānatraya—destiny chose सायण to expound the other three aspects of the वेदस्, viz., the Saṁhitās, the ब्राह्मणस् and the आरण्यकस्. But for his monumental work, much of the original Vedic literature would have remained inscrutable.
Though far removed from the times of the वेदस् chronologically, being brought up in the orthodox tradition as also with his vast knowledge of the सन्स्क्रित् लन्गुअगे and ancient literature, he was ideally suited to this stupendous task.
He was the second son of Māyaṇa and Śrīmatī, Mādhava (Vidyāraṇya) and Bhoganātha being his elder and younger brothers.
Physically he was strong and handsome, well-versed even in the martial arts. As regards his एदुचतिओन् in the traditional scriptures, arts and sciences, he seems to have been trained by his own ड़थेर् first and later by Sarvajña Viṣṇubhaṭṭa (Vidyā-tīrtha) and श्रीकण्ठ उपाध्याय.
He was deeply involved in the training of the princes of the Vijayanagara empire and was also the prime minister for four kings from A. D. 1340 to 1387.
Eight works have been ascribed to his authorship. They are: Subhāṣita-sudhānidhi; Yajñatantrasudhānidhi; Prāyaścittasudhānidhi; Āyurvedasudhā-nidhi; Alaṅkārasudhānidhi; Dhātuvṛtti; Puruṣārthasudhānidhi; Vedārthaprakāśa.
It is the general opinion of Vedic scholars that the last work—detailed commentary on the Vedas—must have been undertaken by a group of scholars under the overall supervision of सायण (and विद्यारण्य). Of course, सायण too must have contributed to it substantially.
The Subhāṣitasudhānidhi is a compendium of pithy sayings on मोरलित्य्, एथिच्स् and general knowledge.
As the very name indicates, the Yajñatantrasudhānidhī deals with the performance of वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्.
The third work, also known as Karmavipāka, deals with prāyaścittas or expiatory rites.
The fourth work on the आयुर्वेद was probably written by Ekāmranātha Paṇḍita at the instance of सायण. It is not available now.
The next work on अलङ्कार or figures of speech was probably authored by his younger brother Bhoganātha. The full text has not been secured so far.
Dhātuvṛtti, the sixth in the series, is an authoritative work on Sanskrit grammar, concentrating on the dhātus (basic roots of verbs). The full text has been edited and printed.
The next work, the Puruṣārthasudhā-nidhi deals in detail with the four puruṣārthas—dharma, अर्थ, काम and mokṣa—and is similar to the treatises on the धर्मशास्त्रस् and the आगमस्.
However, it is the Vedārthaprakāśa, his magnum opus, that has made him immortal in the annals of Vedic literature. It might have been composed during the period A. D. 1360 to 1385.
It should however be noted that he has dealt with only the कर्मकाण्ड part of the वेदस् and has not touched the ज्ञानकाण्ड part (i.e., the उपनिषद्स् or the Vedānta).
It was the encouragement and generous patronage of the king Bukka (rule: A. D. 1354 to 1376) that helped सायण to successfully complete this astounding work. Many contemporary scholars of repute like Pañcāgni Mādhava, Naraharibhaṭṭa, नारायण Vājapeyī, Paṇḍari Dīkṣita and Vāmanabhaṭṭa were also involved in this work, सायण’s contribution being the greatest.
Sāyaṇa is very particular to mention the names of the earlier teachers and commentators like यास्क, आपस्तम्ब, आश्वलायन, पाणिनि, कात्यायन, पतञ्जलि, Bhaṭṭabhāskara Miśra, स्कन्दस्वामिन् and others.
Though his interpretations have sometimes been criticised by modern scholars—both European and Indian—none in his position could have accomplished such a gigantic task in so perfect a manner.
Scholars of religion and philosophy in general, and Hindus in particular, should ever remain deeply indebted to him.
See also VIDYĀRAṆYA.

śayānamūrti
(‘image in the reclining posture’)
------------------------------------------
The images of gods established in temples are generally of three types, of which the śayānamūrtis (in the reclining posture) are the last. According to the Vaikhānasāgama it is only the images of Viṣṇu—as those of रङ्गनाथ and Padmanābha—that are shown as śayāna-mūrtis.
See also MŪRTIŚILPAŚĀSTRA.

sāyujya
(‘getting united [with God]’)
------------------------------------------
In this state of लिबेरतिओन्, the जीव gets merged in the Supreme even as a river merges with the sea or ocean.
See MOKṢA.
